FOR INFLUENTIAL POINTS STUFF GO TO LINE 206
```{r}
data <- read.csv("nba_final.csv")
#summary(data)
data <- data[complete.cases(data[, c(8,9,10,21,26,27,28,29,30,31,32,33,34,45)]), ]
dim(data)
```

```{r}
data$Play <- as.factor(data$Play)
model <- lm(data=data, Salary~G+GS+MP+FT+TRB+AST+STL+BLK+TOV+PF+PTS+
              mean_views+Play+mean_views:Play)#chose mean_views:Play as interaction term because
#it could be interesting to see if an increase in views on wikipedia has a different effect
#on salary if the player has already been in an all star game
e_hat<-resid(model)
y_hat<-fitted(model)
summary(model)
```

```{r}
#apply box-cox on predictors(FT, TRB, AST, TOV, PTS) to fix the constant variance issues
#install.packages("car")
#library(car)
#summary(powerTransform(cbind(data[,c('FT','TRB','AST','TOV', 'PTS')] + 1)))

#apply transfromations on each variable based on results above
data$bcFT <- (data$FT + 1)^(-1/2)
data$bcAST <- (data$AST + 1)^(-1/3)
data$bcTOV <- (data$TOV + 1)^(-1/3)
data$bcPTS <- (data$PTS + 1)^(-1/3)
```



```{r}
#fit a new model using transformed response and predictors
model3 <- lm(lnSalary ~ G + GS + MP + bcFT + TRB + bcAST + STL + BLK + bcTOV + PF + bcPTS +
              lnviews + Play + lnviews:Play, data=data)
summary(model3)

e_hat3 <- resid(model3)
y_hat3 <- fitted(model3)
```


```{r, fig.width=14, fig.height=14}
png("pairs_plot3.png", width = 800, height = 800, res = 100)
pairs(data[, c("G","GS","MP","bcFT","TRB","bcAST","STL","BLK","bcTOV","PF","bcPTS","lnviews")])
dev.off()
```

```{r, echo=F, fig.width=8, fig.height=11}
par(mfrow=c(4,3))
plot(data$lnSalary ~ y_hat3, ylab="lnSalary", xlab="Fitted")
plot(e_hat3 ~ y_hat3, ylab="Residuals", xlab="Fitted")
```


```{r, echo=F, fig.width=8, fig.height=11}
par(mfrow = c(3, 3))

for(i in c("G","GS","MP","bcFT","TRB","bcAST","STL","BLK","bcTOV","PF","bcPTS","lnviews")){
plot(e_hat3 ~ data[,i], ylab="Residuals", xlab= i)
}
```


```{r}
#follow format from worksheet 8
n <- nrow(data)
p <- length(coef(model3))-1

# leverage cutoff
hcut <- 2*(p+1)/n

# cook's distance cutoff
cookcut <- qf(0.5, p+1, n-p-1)

# dffits cutoff
fitcut <- 2*sqrt((p+1)/n)

# dfbeta cutoff
betacut <- 2/sqrt(n)
```

```{r}
# leverage statistic
h_ii <- hatvalues(model3)

# standardized residuals
r_i <- rstandard(model3)

# cook's distance 
D_i <- cooks.distance(model3)

# dffits
dffits_i <- dffits(model3)

# dfbetas
dfbetas_i <- dfbetas(model3)
```

```{r,eval=F}
# which observations are leverage points?
which(h_ii > hcut)

# which observations are regression outliers?
which(r_i > 4 | r_i < -4)

# which observations are influential by cook's distance?
which(D_i > cookcut)

# which observations are influential by dffits?
which(abs(dffits_i) > fitcut)

# which observations are influential by dfbetas?
for(i in 1:8){
  print(paste0("Beta ", i-1))
  print(which(abs(dfbetas_i[,i]) > betacut))    # this checks all betas in a loop
}
```

The model takes these contributions and assumes a higher salary but they were getting paid bottom of the barrel.
